Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National Nitiwul accuses government of buying two VIP aircraft for President in one year 18 November 2026 5:13pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Former Defence Minister Dominic Nitiwul has accused the government of acquiring two VIP aircraft for the President within a year, questioning the purchase of an Airbus H175 helicopter alongside the Falcon 6X executive jet.
Contributing to the debate on the 2027 Budget Statement in Parliament on Thursday, November 19, 2026, Mr Nitiwul argued that the Airbus H175 was designed for civilian rather than military purposes.
Referring to paragraphs in the Budget Statement, he said the helicopter should be considered alongside the Falcon 6X when assessing the government's aircraft acquisitions.
“On page 158, paragraph 475, this aircraft that you went and bought, Airbus H175, it's meant for civilian purposes. It's not a military aircraft. Same thing as 168. It's a civilian-branded aircraft. So you bought two VIP aircraft for the President. Two. In one year,” he stated.
Mr Nitiwul also accused members of the governing NDC of applying different standards to the current administration and the previous NPP government over presidential aircraft procurement.
He said the NDC had criticised the previous government over its attempt to acquire a new presidential jet, despite what he described as the absence of a formal request for a replacement aircraft at the time.
“These are the same people who, when I had not even requested a new aircraft, insulted the President, insulted myself, blasted me, made me look like I didn't know what I was doing, made me look like I was a fool,” he stated.
The government has confirmed the acquisition of a Falcon 6X executive jet and four helicopters for the Ghana Air Force as part of a broader retooling programme.
Parliament approved the aircraft procurement on December 4, 2025.
The debate on the 2027 Budget Statement is expected to continue in Parliament.
